summary: Sound stage 2 that follows REWRITE_READ section 1 exactly (keep the proven 2-CTA/SM cp.async ring, fold combine via ticket, stream-K tiles), with no rules problem; but the decode_32 'L2/TLB locality' bandwidth-recovery claim is unsupported because reference.py builds the page table from a global randperm, so the decode_32 M2 target (<=222 us) is unlikely and should be read from the in-process diagnostics, not the headline.
justification: Profile (FINDINGS, job 698d4cd3838c4a63): full decode_16 = splitkv_attn_kernel 111.8 + splitkv_combine_kernel 8.2 + pre-attn 2.1 us (floor 63.2); decode_32 = 245.9 + 8.4 + 2.0 us (floor 126.4). Kernel A is 92-96% of each shape, at ~2.94 and ~2.67 TB/s. The ticket fold removes one launch and the separate B kernel, but the LSE merge still runs as a serialized tail in the last-arriving CTA per request. That CTA reads about grid/B slots x (16x64+32) fp32: roughly 17 slots (~70 KB) at B=16 and 8 slots at B=32, all L2-hot. So the realistic net saving is ~4-7 us, not the full 8. splitkv-pdl-attn-to-combine was neutral, so the launch gap itself is small; the saving comes from B's own body. Stream-K over 64-token tiles removes the 1024-chunk tail, which is about 4.7 items/CTA at B=16 and about 9.5 at B=32. But splitkv-chunk2048-batch32 (doubling item size, so a worse tail) came out neutral, which says the tail is not the decode_32 limiter. WEAKEST LINK: the claim that contiguous per-CTA tile ranges restore decode_32 bandwidth through L2/TLB locality. reference.py lines 187-192 fill page_table from torch.randperm(total), so KV row addresses are uniformly scattered over the whole ~655 MB cache whatever order the page table is walked in. Contiguity only helps the 4 B/token page-table reads (~1.5% of bytes). The 2.94 -> 2.67 TB/s drop is more plausibly a TLB-reach or DRAM-page effect of the doubled random footprint, which stream-K does not touch. Expect M1 on both shapes, M2 plausible at decode_16 (<=108 needs -11 us: ~5-7 from the ticket plus the tail), M2 at decode_32 (<=222, -32 us) unlikely (~-8 to -12 realistic), and M3 (<=1.5x floor, ~3.2 TB/s effective on random 128 B gathers) not reachable by this stage's changes. The milestones are readable from profile top_kernels, since v2 is a single named kernel replacing A+B. The expected directions match TASK.md: the full-layer weight of 16 applies only to decode_16/32, and every other shape is gated out.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: the incumbent being replaced, not a confounder. v2 keeps its ring and math byte-identical, so a v2-vs-A+B delta is attributable to the split and epilogue only. The FINDINGS caveat applies: full decode_32 headline rows have shown a scoring artifact before (full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv 'gained' 1.14x with an unchanged kernel A), so judge decode_32 by kernel time.

fused-preattention-triton: _pre_attention_kernel produces the FP8 q that v2 consumes, unchanged. It is a launch-sequence neighbour only. With B gone, v2 is directly followed by the graph end, so no interaction is expected.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup / fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / ab-tune-batch-gate: the pairing predicate already excludes splitkv shapes ('and not splitkv'), so they are not on this path and do not confound.
sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv / sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: sliding-only and gated out of the full decode path. Their shapes should be flat; any headline movement there is noise.
interference: No companion is warranted. The spec already builds the needed controls in-process at import time: eager timings at synthetic B=16 and B=32 x 80000 of stage-1 A+B, stream-K without the ticket (+B), stream-K with the ticket, and 5 stages. Those separate the two sub-changes (work split vs epilogue fold) and the stages knob on the same GPU, in the same run, with the same inputs, which a separate okc run could not do more cleanly. No landed hypothesis shares this kernel's code path except the incumbent it replaces, so an ab-revert has nothing to isolate. For a rewrite, the next stage is the follow-up. Ask the builder to print those diagnostics as per-kernel µs and TB/s (bytes = sum(seq_b) x 256 B), so the decode_32 locality claim is directly confirmed or refuted by the 'stream-K no ticket' vs 'stage-1 A' line.
rules_flags: No rule violation found. The ticket is a module-level int32[64] allocated at import, not derived from inputs. Master already uses the same pattern (_COUNTERS). Workspace sizes come from grid (device) and batch (shape) only. No host sync in kernel_fn. The self-check, image check and diagnostics run at import, outside the timed call. load_inline is already used by master, which passed the static checker.

Correctness hazard (not a rule): the fence order must be all threads store the partial -> __threadfence() -> __syncthreads() -> one thread atomicAdd. The spec omits the __syncthreads. Without it, thread 0 can publish the ticket before other warps' partial stores are visible. The last CTA must also read the slots with ld.global.cg/volatile (never __ldg/.nc), or it can see stale L1 lines.

Every-key: the zero-filled page indices past each request end (index 0 -> row 0) must be masked to -inf in the scores, not just zero-filled. Otherwise row 0's key is attended up to 63 times per request tail, which the seq % 64 in 1..7 self-check cases should catch.

nseg_b = 0 (a zero-length request) would leave that output row unwritten. Scored and test decode lengths are >= 1 (clamp(1, ...)), so this is safe as written. Add a guard or a self-check assert anyway.
Sticky-fault risk is acknowledged: an illegal-address fault in the canary poisons the context, so the fallback cannot run. The 'first run is okc check' rule handles this; keep it.
open_questions: Is the decode_32 bandwidth drop (2.94 -> 2.67 TB/s) a TLB-reach effect of the 2x random footprint? If so, stream-K cannot fix it, and stage 3 should instead test request/tile ordering that keeps concurrently active CTAs within a bounded slice of the cache (impossible with a randperm page table), or accept ~2.7 TB/s and stop at M2.
Does the last-arriver merge at B=16 (~17 slots per request on one CTA) add a visible serialized tail? Compare 'stream-K with ticket' vs 'stream-K no ticket + B' in the diagnostics.

splitkv-full-line-gather-mapping (unproven-vs-best at 1.416x, gained on full decode_16/32) changes the same issue_tile mapping that v2 keeps 'exactly'. Should stage 3 stack it onto v2, since v2 freezes the stage-1 gather?
Two load_inline modules (v1 fallback + v2) at about 45 s each, plus eager diagnostics at B=32 x 80000 for 4 variants: confirm the total stays well inside the 15-minute budget with the 16 tests.
